question: By July 6, 2016, what evidence showed that West Calumet residents had received the soil-test results for their own homes?
receipt_rule: Require a Zone 1 household, its own property-specific soil result, and an acknowledgment or recipient-side account placing receipt on or before July 6. Distinguish mailing, leaving a flyer, institutional receipt, relocation notices, and report publication from household receipt. One household can establish only its own experience.

sources.author: EPA
sources.locator: November 2014 fact sheet, p. 1, Upcoming work
lines: EPA planned further sampling at public housing properties and expected the results to identify yards for cleanup.
EPA said officials would meet each property owner before excavation to discuss the work.

sources.author: EPA Region 5
lines: EPA announced plans to cover bare dirt in West Calumet housing complex yards and around a playground.
EPA reported that its staff and ATSDR had been visiting residents door to door with advice about reducing exposure to lead.
The release directed residents to the city health department for information about children's blood testing.

sources.author: City of East Chicago
sources.locator: City timeline pp. 1–2, May 24, June 29 and July 11 entries. Preserve the year printed in the date column.
lines: The city timeline dates its first access to West Calumet address-level soil contamination documents to May 24, 2016.
The city records a June 29 canvass distributing information about lead and blood testing.
The timeline describes July 11–14 mailing of individual soil results. Its date column says July 11, 2015, between entries for July 5 and July 14, 2016.

sources.author: Janet Pope, EPA
sources.locator: Declaration filed in 2:14-cv-00312, document 24-4, paragraphs 58 and 60
lines: Pope reported that EPA staff left lead-prevention flyers during door-to-door outreach at the housing complex on July 5, 2016.
Pope said EPA shared copies of the results letters mailed to residents with city, school and park officials on July 13.

sources.author: EPA Region 5
lines: EPA's declaration says it gave the city and the housing authority validated results for most housing-complex soils on May 24, 2016.

sources.author: Annie Ropeik interview with former resident Akeeshea Daniels, NPR transcript via WLRN
lines: Daniels recalled receiving a letter telling her to move. She described surprise and concern about where she and her children could live.

sources.author: Former West Calumet resident, public comment to EPA
sources.locator: Letter dated January 14, 2019, opening paragraphs; admitted only to retrospective pack
lines: A former resident wrote that in 2016 they received a letter from the mayor asking their family to relocate because of contamination.
The commenter described difficulty finding replacement housing in East Chicago.

sources.author: US District Court, Northern District of Indiana
sources.locator: Rolan v. Atlantic Richfield, document 152, pp. 3–4, communication of soil testing results
lines: The court recounted that EPA began mailing residents their soil-test results in early June 2016.
The court identified a July 8, 2016 letter to Rolan advising that the property qualified for soil cleanup.

sources.author: US District Court, same litigation
sources.locator: Rolan, document 169, institutional notice and relocation
lines: A later order puts provision of soil-test results to the city and the housing authority on May 26, 2016.

sources.author: EPA
sources.locator: User-supplied Zone 1 page, Results of Lead and Arsenic Testing and page revision date
lines: EPA's Zone 1 page describes front- and back-yard sampling at all residences from December 2014 into 2015 and links a results spreadsheet with identifying information removed.
